nodes.title: Equal values, different representations
nodes.body: A fraction represents a quotient with a nonzero denominator. Multiplying its numerator and denominator by the same nonzero integer preserves its value. Reducing changes representation; it does not explain why an answer solves a task.
nodes.exercise: Explain why10/12 and5/6 have equal values.
nodes.hint: Compare the two cross products10*6 and5*12.

nodes.title: A worked common denominator
nodes.body: Rewrite each summand using a common denominator before adding. Then check which common factors can be cancelled.
nodes.exercise: Explain each equality in the worked example.
nodes.hint: Distinguish adding fractions from multiplying their denominators.
nodes.worked: For3/8+1/4, rewrite1/4 as2/8; add to get5/8. Its numerator and denominator have no common factor larger than1.

nodes.title: Calculate, then check the exact task
nodes.body: The supported task is1/2+1/3=N/D over rational numbers. Enter10/12, use REDUCE if helpful, and observe the changed representation. REDUCE clears current checking; press CHECK separately before Save and SEND. Local calculator use is permitted for this practice and remains disclosed to the teacher.
nodes.exercise: Submit a fraction equal to1/2+1/3. Write the common-denominator argument, and identify any calculator or hint you used.
nodes.hint: Use denominator6:1/2=3/6 and1/3=2/6. Explain why these replacements preserve value. REDUCE only edits the representation; a later CHECK addresses the exact addition task.

nodes.title: Find the illegal rule
nodes.body: A learner proposes adding numerators and denominators separately, obtaining2/5 for1/2+1/3. Give an exact comparison that identifies the error. A calculator answer alone is not the requested explanation.
nodes.exercise: Write a counterexample and name the invalid operation.
nodes.hint: Compare both proposed values after expressing them with denominator30.

nodes.title: Transfer cancellation to a variable
nodes.body: For rational t, compare(t*t-9)/(t-3) with t+3. State the original expression's domain, factor the numerator, and justify every cancellation. Decide what happens at t=3. This written argument requires teacher review.
nodes.exercise: State the original rational domain, factor the numerator and justify cancellation under its nonzero assumption. At t=3 compare whether each displayed expression is defined; equality does not restore an excluded input.

nodes.title: Later independent reconstruction
nodes.body: Without copying the worked example, explain why common denominators preserve fraction values. Give your own pair of unequal fractions exposing the add-numerators-and-denominators rule, then justify a valid sum. This is written reasoning; the exact numeric checker cannot certify it.
nodes.exercise: Write a new response for independent teacher review.

learningGoals: Distinguish equal rational values from the form of a fraction
Use a common denominator and factors to justify equality
Separate a local calculator result from checking and an independent written argument
Retain original domain restrictions after cancelling a variable factor
notationGuide: N/D uses a nonzero positive denominator in the current numeric UI.
REDUCE is a local advisory edit; CHECK is a separate exact task check.
Written variable reasoning remains opaque work for a human assessment.
